source.work: Clean Architecture (R. C. Martin, 2017) and Agile Software Development (R. C. Martin, 2002)
source.paraphrase: The dependency graph of components has no cycles. A cycle means the components cannot be tested, released, or understood apart.

invariants.why: A new import cycle forces a reader to load every module in the loop before any one of them makes sense, and a change in one module can break the others in an order the typechecker will not explain.
invariants.fixHint: Break the cycle with a one-way import. Move the shared type to a third module, or keep the back edge as a dynamic import() that loads only after both modules have initialized.
invariants.avoid: import type and a specifier list that is entirely type are erased and are not a cycle. require() and export from are value edges. An existing cycle may stay; this rule denies only a cycle this edit creates or enlarges.

source.locator: Single Responsibility Principle, the module as the unit of change
source.paraphrase: A module should have one reason to change. A file that keeps growing is standing in for several modules.

invariants.why: A file past this size is the usual stand-in for a module that does several jobs. Callers cannot tell which part they depend on, and a change for one job risks the others.
invariants.fixHint: Move a cohesive group of declarations into a new module and import it one way. Leave the file at or below the ceiling.
invariants.avoid: Packing many statements onto one line does not shrink the count. Comments and blank lines do not raise it. A file already over the ceiling may be edited as long as the count does not grow.

source.locator: Single Responsibility Principle, the published surface of a module
source.paraphrase: The public surface of a module should be small enough that a caller can know which names are the contract.

invariants.why: A long export list is a second stand-in for a module with several jobs: every name is a promise to callers, including types.
invariants.fixHint: Group the names into smaller modules, or stop exporting names that only this file uses.
invariants.avoid: One export { a, b, c } clause still counts each name. Overloads of one function count once. A surface already over the ceiling may stay if this edit does not add a name.

source.work: A Metrics Suite for Object Oriented Design (S. R. Chidamber and C. F. Kemerer, 1994) and Design Patterns (E. Gamma, R. Helm, R. Johnson, J. Vlissides, 1994)
source.locator: Depth of Inheritance Tree; favor object composition over class inheritance
source.paraphrase: A deep class hierarchy is harder to reason about than a shallow one. Composition is the usual replacement once the chain is no longer a small specialization.

invariants.why: Each extends hop adds behavior the reader has to find in another class. Past a short chain, a change in the base is a change in every descendant, and the descendant's own job is no longer visible in its file.
invariants.fixHint: Replace a hop with a field that holds the collaborator, or stop the chain at the ceiling. This warning does not block the edit.
invariants.avoid: interface extends is not a class hop. extends React.Component, a mixin() call, and an unresolved name count as one hop and stop. implements is not counted.
